topic: A productive plot is not necessarily a fair comparison
grammarFocus: 学术论证的限定、因果、对比与证据范围
title: A productive plot is not necessarily a fair comparison
instructions: 原创学术微训练；场景、机构与数值均为虚构模拟，不是事实报道或官方试题。先独立阅读答题，再用原句核对限定、比较与因果。短篇专项不能替代完整陌生测评。
passage:
A. In a fictional agricultural class, students compared two vegetable plots. One received compost and the other did not. At harvest, the compost plot produced more kilograms of vegetables. The class newsletter announced that the treatment had increased yield. The tutor asked whether the observed difference could be attributed to the treatment alone.

B. The plots were not equally exposed to sunlight. A wall shaded the untreated plot during the afternoon, and water from a nearby path drained into the other plot. Because the treatment and location varied together, the comparison could not isolate the effect of compost. Measuring the harvest carefully did not compensate for an unfair experimental arrangement.

C. The tutor proposed dividing the garden into smaller sections and randomly assigning treatment within several matched pairs. Each pair would contain neighbouring sections with similar exposure. Random allocation would reduce systematic selection by the students, while replication would show whether differences persisted across sections. Neither procedure guaranteed identical starting conditions, so soil characteristics would still be recorded.

D. The class also reconsidered the meaning of yield. A heavier harvest might include more damaged vegetables. Weighing only the marketable portion would answer a different question from weighing everything grown. For this teaching project, the team decided to record both total mass and usable mass, with a written rule for classifying damage before seeing the final results.

E. The second trial would take a full growing season, so the class could not publish a firm causal conclusion immediately. Instead, it described the first comparison as exploratory and explained the redesigned procedure. That account was less dramatic than the original headline but more useful to a reader considering a similar experiment. The important progress was a clearer question and a fairer design, rather than a stronger claim unsupported by the available observations. The newsletter kept the original result visible beside the correction.

questions.prompt: Why did the original comparison not isolate the treatment?

The class had randomly assigned every section.
